encounters.cc: Worsening symmetric joint pain over past 4 months with new knee involvement

lines: Worsening symmetric joint pain over past 4 months with new knee involvement
A 33-year-old female with hypothyroidism and alcohol use disorder in remission returns for follow-up of progressive joint symptoms with new knee involvement over four months.
She describes stiffness in the morning that lasts over an hour and gradually improves throughout the day.
The discomfort began in her wrists and now affects the small joints of her hands and knees, all of which feel swollen and tender.
The symptoms are symmetric.
She denies any fevers, skin rashes, or prior trauma.

On exam, there is synovial thickening and tenderness over the bilateral metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints.

encounters.cc: Progressive joint stiffness over 8 months with significant functional impairment in daily activities

lines: Progressive joint stiffness over 8 months with significant functional impairment in daily activities

The patient is a 34-year-old female with hypothyroidism and history of alcohol use disorder in remission who returns for rheumatology follow-up regarding joint symptoms initially evaluated in January 2020.
She reports that the stiffness is particularly pronounced in the morning and can last over an hour before it begins to ease with movement.
The discomfort is most noticeable in her wrists, hands, and ankles.
She describes difficulty gripping items, turning doorknobs, and typing at her job as a writer.
She also mentions fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and a recent unintended weight loss of 3 kilograms over the last few months.
She denies any trauma, rash, visual symptoms, or recent illnesses.
Active Problem List:
- Rheumatoid arthritis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Hypothyroidism
- History of alcohol use disorder (in remission)
- Tonsillectomy (age 8)
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 21)
Home Medications:
- Levothyroxine 88 mcg PO daily
NKDA
There is no family history of autoimmune disease.
She does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits.
She appears well but somewhat fatigued.
Her wrists are slightly swollen and tender to palpation with limited range of motion.
The second and third metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally are also swollen and tender.
There is no redness or warmth over the joints.
The distal interphalangeal joints are not affected.
Both ankles show mild swelling without erythema or warmth.
The remainder of the physical exam is unremarkable.
Laboratory evaluation reveals normocytic anemia and elevated inflammatory markers.
Radiographs of the hands demonstrate periarticular osteopenia but no erosions.
